title: Smooth principal neighbourhood from regularity and finite separable residue
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open. Put $S=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)$ with the $k$-algebra structure induced by $f$, and let $\iota_U:\operatorname{Spec}S\to X$ be the canonical open immersion onto $U$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] [def-weil-open-immersion]. Assume $S$ is of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime, put $x=\iota_U(\mathfrak q)$, and assume the local ring $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme] and its residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is finite separable over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Then there exists $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $S_g$ is a smooth $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], where $S_g$ is localization at $\{1,g,g^2,\ldots\}$. For such a $g$, put $D(g)=\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}S:g\notin\mathfrak p\}$ and $V=\iota_U(D(g))$, with its open subscheme structure. The canonical map $\operatorname{Spec}S_g\to X$ identifies $\operatorname{Spec}S_g$ with $V$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$: the structural map on the source is induced by $k\to S\to S_g$ and equals $f$ composed with this canonical map. Moreover $x\in V$ and $f|_V:V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. There is no dimension, integrality, normality or perfection assumption.

source.place: Tag 00TV, lemma-separable-smooth, implication (2) to (1), and Tag 00TB, definition-smooth-at-prime; geometric interpretation via Schemes Tag 01I3, lemma-standard-open-affine, and Morphisms Tag 01V6, lemma-smooth-characterize.

proof.text: Put $K=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. The assumed finite separable extension is separable also in the general-field sense used by 00TV. Indeed, for every finitely generated intermediate field $k\subset K\prime\subset K$, every element of $K\prime$ is algebraic over $k$ with the same separable minimal polynomial over $k$ as in $K$. Thus $K\prime/k$ is separable algebraic. Its empty family is a transcendence basis: $k[\varnothing]=k$ injects into $K\prime$ and $K\prime/k$ is algebraic. Consequently every such $K\prime/k$ is separably generated, exactly the definition of separability of $K/k$.

source.place: definition-separable-field-extension, Tag 030O; empty transcendence basis for an algebraic extension; Fields definition-separable, Tag 09H1

proof.text: Apply the implication from regularity to smoothness at $\mathfrak q$ in [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-separable-residue-smooth]: $S$ is finite type over the field $k$, the specified local ring is regular, and step 1 verifies the residue-field separability hypothesis. By [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal], smoothness at this prime means precisely that some $g\notin\mathfrak q$ makes $k\to S\to S_g$ smooth. Choose this $g$.

For any such $g$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime] identifies $V=\iota_U(D(g))$ as an affine open of $X$ and its section ring with $S_g$ by the restriction localization $S\to\mathcal O_X(V)$. Hence the corresponding affine isomorphism $e:\operatorname{Spec}S_g\xrightarrow{\sim}V$ has composite to $U=\operatorname{Spec}S$ equal to $\operatorname{Spec}(S\to S_g)$: both induce that restriction map on sections. The contravariant functoriality and uniqueness in [def-weil-affine-spectrum] now give $f|_V\circ e=\operatorname{Spec}(k\to S\to S_g)$, since the original $k$-algebra structure on $S$ was induced by $f$. Also $g\notin\mathfrak q$ gives $\mathfrak q\in D(g)$, hence $x\in V$.

source.place: lemma-standard-open-affine, Tag 01I3; lemma-spec-sheaves, Tag 01HV; canonical restriction and functoriality of Spec

proof.text: The smooth ring map $k\to S_g$ gives a smooth morphism $h:\operatorname{Spec}S_g\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine]. Step 3 gives $h=f|_V\circ e$. Apply clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] to the source isomorphism $e$ and the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}k$. It follows that $f|_V$ is smooth, with the asserted structural map. This works for every $g$ satisfying the algebraic conclusion.
